clue.text: Result of weaving, by one of three men in a boat on the river

parts.words: one of three men in a boat
parts.note: Harris is one of the trio, with George and J, in Jerome K Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat
the Tweed is the river along the Scottish–English border

explanation.surface: A piece of cloth produced by a character from a Victorian boating novel, out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: HARRIS TWEED is a cloth hand-woven in the Outer Hebrides, so it is literally the result of weaving.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous cloth is a woven fabric, so it is a product of the loom.

clue.text: Old silver, limited edition

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
the word edition cut short gives its usual abbreviation, ed

explanation.surface: An antique piece of silverware made in a small print run.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly people are said to be advanced in years, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Hurry, then flag

definitions.meaning: a flag is an iris; the marsh plant of the same kind shares the name

explanation.surface: Someone races along and then tires.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means a hasty dash and also a waterside reed, as the flag iris is.

clue.text: Dog Sybil's about to tease, you'll hear

annotationWithheld.why: Dog Sybil's about to tease, you'll hear (6): SETTER is the dog, but no reading of 'Sybil's about to tease' sounds like SETTER without a word doing two jobs; no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Dog Sybil's about to tease, you'll hear

clue.text: Protective wear for New Zealand shoe-shine boy?

parts.note: Wellington is the capital of New Zealand, standing in for the country
Boots was the old name for the hotel servant who cleaned guests' shoes

explanation.surface: A question about what a Kiwi bootblack wears on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOTS is the old British name for the hotel servant who polished guests' footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber knee-high footwear keeps the legs dry, so it is protective clothing.

clue.text: There's a book in it

parts.note: the letters of the word there's can be rearranged into the name of an Old Testament book, so a book sits inside it

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a story would make a good novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a story worth writing up; cryptically the six letters of THERE'S rearrange into an Old Testament book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Esther is one of the historical books of the Hebrew Bible.

clue.text: Through which latecomers hope to gain admittance?

definitions.text: Through which latecomers hope to gain admittance?

parts.words: Through which latecomers hope to gain admittance?
parts.note: latecomers are not those who arrive late but the late, the dead, hoping to be let into heaven

explanation.surface: People arriving late hope a door will still let them in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latecomers' suggests tardy guests, but 'the late' are the dead, seeking entry to heaven at St Peter's gate.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular tradition says heaven's entrance is made of pearl, guarded by St Peter.

clue.text: Pilfer — that's Samuel Smiles' advice

definitions.meaning: to steal, i.e. take without asking
Samuel Smiles wrote the Victorian bestseller Self-Help, urging readers to improve themselves

explanation.surface: Stealing is recommended by a Victorian moralist.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Smiles was a Victorian Scottish author whose book Self-Help preached self-reliance.
explanation.definitionFit: To take freely for yourself, without permission, is to steal; it is also the self-reliance a Victorian writer preached.

clue.text: Holiday an inevitable necessity, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word meaning destiny is to be taken as spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: fate is what must inevitably happen

explanation.surface: A day off is something we're told is unavoidable.
explanation.definitionFit: A fête is a festival or feast day, an occasion of celebration.

clue.text: Changing tyre is vital for good all-round performance

indicators.note: the letters of tyre is vital are being changed around into a new order

explanation.surface: Swapping tyres is said to be key to a car's overall performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' rearranges TYRE IS VITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Adaptability, being good at many things, makes for a performance that is strong all round.

clue.text: Fall over rubbish out East

indicators.note: the compass letter is to be left out of the slang word for nonsense

parts.note: tripe is slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles over litter on the east side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops E from TRIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: To stumble and tumble over something is to lose your footing, a synonym.

clue.text: Intimate you'll have one ally fewer when the leader is removed

definitions.text: you'll have one ally fewer when the leader is removed
definitions.meaning: dropping the first letter leaves a phrase meaning to be deprived of a pal

explanation.surface: A warning that sacking the chief will cost you a supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the initial C and the phrase becomes LOSE FRIEND, which is to have one ally fewer.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidant is someone you are very near to in affection.

clue.text: Inappropriate number for the ball?

parts.note: a number here is a piece played at a dance, and square means old-fashioned, hardly right for a smart ball

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a dress or a tune is unsuitable for a formal dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' is slang for unfashionable, and a 'number' is a dance tune; there is also a nod to square numbers and a round ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A folk dance for four couples arranged in a quadrangle; its rustic style would seem out of place at a grand ball.

clue.text: Instructions for providing about a hundred mince pies

parts.note: re means about or concerning
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up, so the letters of pies are chopped into a new order

explanation.surface: Directions for making a large batch of Christmas mince pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince' looks like part of the Christmas pies, but it is the signal to chop up the letters of the word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking directions are a series of steps telling a cook how to make a dish.

clue.text: Rob seed to stock it?

parts.note: the letters of rob seed rearrange to name a garden plot, and a stock is also a garden flower that could fill it

explanation.surface: A thief steals seeds to fill a garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: An old-style clue: ROB SEED rearranges into the answer with no separate signal, and 'stock' is both 'fill' and a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowerbed planted with roses is the plot the clue imagines being filled.

clue.text: Head of steam inducing movement of rollers

indicators.note: only the leading letter of the word steam is taken

parts.note: urging means pressing or persuading, so inducing

explanation.surface: Building up steam to get heavy rollers moving.
explanation.walkthrough: Rollers are big ocean waves, not machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Waves heaving forward in a swell are said to be swelling powerfully onward, a synonym for their motion.

clue.text: This ice is black

parts.note: put this word in front of ice and you get a black sweet made from a root

explanation.surface: A claim that some frozen water is dark.
explanation.walkthrough: Add ICE to the answer and you get LIQUORICE, a black sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcoholic drink, which joined to ice makes the black confection.

clue.text: Writer seen to dash over there

parts.note: to run is to dash
yon is an old word for over there

explanation.surface: An author is spotted hurrying across the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Damon Runyon was the American author of the Broadway stories behind Guys and Dolls.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon Runyon was an American author of short stories.

clue.text: Lurking danger from which sheik's agents ran

indicators.note: the answer's letters come out of the following words, which must be rearranged to produce it

explanation.surface: An oil sheik's spies flee from some hidden peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from which' signals that SHEIKS AGENTS RAN is rearranged; the possessive 's here does count as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A treacherous friend is a hidden threat, like a serpent lying unseen in the lawn.

clue.text: Touch, with hesitation, part of beetle

parts.note: to feel is to touch
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Gingerly prodding a beetle's body.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is the sensory organ an insect uses to probe its surroundings.

clue.text: Lira to change in Venice

indicators.note: the letters of lira and to are changed around into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller exchanges Italian currency in Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges LIRA TO. The Rialto was Venice's commercial and money-changing district, so the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice's old market and exchange quarter by its famous bridge was where money changed hands.

clue.text: Equestrienne princess a late starter-shows temper

parts.note: Princess Anne is a noted horsewoman who rode at the Olympics

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word late is wanted

explanation.surface: A princess who rides shows a flash of anger after a late start.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Anne, the British monarch's sister, rode for Britain at the 1976 Olympics. 'Temper' is the metalworker's sense, not anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Heating and slowly cooling metal or glass to toughen it is how a smith hardens it.

clue.text: Hoped to draw something from the bank

definitions.text: Hoped to draw something from the bank

parts.words: Hoped to draw something from the bank
parts.note: the bank is a riverbank, and drawing something out of it is fishing with rod and line

explanation.surface: Someone wished to withdraw some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The bank is a riverbank, not a lender; 'angled for' also means hoped for.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishing with a rod is done from the riverbank, and to fish for something is also to hope for it.

clue.text: 21 down, maybe favouring this. approach, with Princess and two bishops in Gateshead

parts.note: Di is Princess Diana
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, given twice
taken as written
the head of the word gate is its first letter

explanation.surface: An angler on a trip to a north-east English town with royalty and clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: Dibbing is a fishing method, dapping bait on the surface. Gateshead is a town by Newcastle, but here it is read as 'gate's head', G.
explanation.definitionFit: Dibbing is an angling technique of bobbing bait lightly on the water, so an approach that someone who fished might favour.

clue.text: One military force to question in the Middle East

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
RA is the Royal Artillery
Q is the abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: A soldier is sent to interrogate someone in the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gulf state on the Tigris and Euphrates lies in the region named.

clue.text: I leave right after the Russian

parts.note: to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone says they will set off in pursuit of a man from Moscow.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Russian male name, borne by Stravinsky and Prince Igor of the opera.

clue.text: Knock out — it's crazy to get up

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word for mad is read from bottom to top

parts.note: nuts is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone raging wildly rises from the canvas after a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get up' reverses NUTS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To daze someone with a blow is to make them senseless, a synonym.

clue.text: Navigational aids for Noah's ark?

parts.note: the ark sailed on the Flood, so its lamps would be the lights of the deluge

explanation.surface: A question about the lamps that guided Noah's boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as FLOOD LIGHTS: lamps for a vessel afloat on the biblical deluge.
explanation.definitionFit: Powerful lamps for lighting stadiums, punningly the beacons a deluge-borne vessel would need.

clue.text: Small boy in jail

explanation.surface: A young lad is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The nick' is everyday British slang for a prison or police station.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet form of Nicholas, and a slang word for a cell or prison.

clue.text: Cheat, taking another's part without demur? Thinking of it!

parts.note: to con is to cheat

indicators.note: means outside: the word for taking sides goes around the hesitation

parts.note: siding is taking someone's side
er is a hesitant demurral

explanation.surface: Someone thinks of swindling by backing a rival without objection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here has its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'Thinking of it!' plays on the cheat weighing up the scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh something up is to give it thought, a synonym.
